title: Finite-chart monoscheme components, generic lattices and dense toric realizations
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $(M,\mathcal M)$ a fine torsion-free monoscheme with a finite affine cover [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization], with monoid spectra and localization as in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Put $X=k[M]$. The underlying space of $M$ is finite. Every point $x$ has a unique maximal generalization $\eta(x)$, and the nonempty sets $M_\eta=\{x:\eta(x)=\eta\}$ are the finitely many clopen irreducible connected components [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Each monoid affine chart lies in one $M_\eta$. For every chart $\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P\subset M_\eta$, its group completion identifies canonically with the generic stalk $L_\eta=\mathcal M_\eta$, a finitely generated torsion-free abelian group admitting a finite integral basis. The chart algebra $k[P]$ is a domain generated as a $k$-algebra by $e^{p_1},\ldots,e^{p_n}$ whenever $p_1,\ldots,p_n$ generate $P$.

Realization gives a clopen decomposition $X=\coprod_\eta X_\eta$, $X_\eta=k[M_\eta]$, and $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Each $X_\eta$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], and these are exactly the connected components of $X$. In a chart with the above generators put $a=\sum_i p_i$, with $a=0$ for an empty list. Then $P[a^{-1}]=L_\eta$ and the map $k[P]_{e^a}\longrightarrow k[L_\eta]$, $e^p/(e^a)^n\longmapsto e^{p-na}$, is an isomorphism compatible with the localization gluing. It identifies $D(e^a)$ in every chart of $X_\eta$ with the same nonempty dense irreducible open subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}k[L_\eta]$. The empty monoscheme is allowed and gives the empty realization with zero connected components.

source.place: Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.4(i)--(ii), 3.1.9, Remark 3.1.10(ii), Proposition 3.2.2 and 3.2.4, printed pp.98--100,103; affine domain input in Lemma 3.2.12(ii), p.104. Re-split of returned parent Steps 1--4. No Stacks tag states this monoscheme gluing result.

proof.text: Choose the finite affine atlas in Fine.finiteCover. For each chart choose a finite generating tuple. The face-generator equality and complement equality in monoidPrime_minimal_neighborhood show that two primes with the same subset of excluded generators have equal complements and hence are equal. This injects the chart spectrum into the finite power set of the generator indices. Transport finiteness through the chart homeomorphism and use the surjection from the finite disjoint union of atlas opens onto M. Finally ConnectedComponents.mk is surjective, so the component quotient is finite. The empty atlas case is included by the same surjectivity argument.

The empty monoid prime specializes to every prime: induct on the topology generated by principal opens. Hence every affine chart is nonempty irreducible and connected, and is contained in one connected-component fibre. Monoid spectra are T0 because the basic opens distinguish different prime carriers; T0 descends from the atlas. For a ToricComponent C, use the defining specification of its genericPoint from def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization. Given a chart U in its component, the image eta of the empty prime generalizes C.genericPoint, because C.genericPoint belongs to U. Every other affine chart V in this component contains C.genericPoint, so openness of V implies that it also contains eta. Thus eta satisfies the same defining specification as C.genericPoint, and its uniqueness gives eta=C.genericPoint. Every point x of the component has such a chart U. Consequently C.genericPoint specializes to every x in its fibre. Conversely specialization stays in a connected component, so the fibre is exactly the closure of C.genericPoint. It is therefore closed, irreducible and connected. Chart connectedness and the affine atlas make it open as well. If z generalizes C.genericPoint, it lies in the same fibre and is also specialized by C.genericPoint, so T0 gives equality. This proves the unique maximal-generalization clause. Connectedness bounds every irreducible set by one such fibre; maximality of irreducible components and irreducibility of each fibre identify their range with irreducibleComponents. These arguments are vacuous for empty M.

source.place: VIII Remark 3.1.4(i) and Remark 3.1.10(ii), printed pp.98--100

proof.text: Apply generic_chart_completion for the canonical generic-stalk equivalence and, on every component chart U, fineness of its intrinsic section monoid P_U and the completion equivalence e_U : P_U^gp ≃ L with e_U(of p)=degree p. Choose a chart containing the component generic point and use the already proved affineOpen_component to regard it as a component chart. Finite generation passes from P_U to its Grothendieck group (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.instFG), and then through e_U to L. The hM condition at the generic point implies injectivity of every positive power map on L: apply it to x/y when x^n=y^n. On Additive L, Mathlib supplies the finite torsion-free integer-module instances. Module.basisOfFiniteTypeTorsionFree' gives a basis indexed by Fin r, and its equivFun, converted back to multiplicative notation, yields the required L ≃ Multiplicative (Fin r → ℤ).

source.place: VIII 3.1.9 and 3.2.4, printed pp.99,103; finite basis input also VI 3.7(a), p.75

proof.text: For every component chart, use generic_chart_completion to obtain its intrinsic fineness and e_U. Injectivity into the completion gives a CancelCommMonoid structure. The formula e_U(of p)=degree p makes degree injective. Positive power injectivity of the generic lattice therefore implies the same property for P_U. The affine monoid unique-products instance (the multiplicative form of lem-trf-affine-monoid-unique-sums) and the monoid-algebra domain instance (the multiplicative form of lem-trf-unique-sums-algebra-domain) prove that k[P_U] is a domain. For any given generating tuple p, let A be the algebra adjoin of its monomials. Submonoid.closure_induction shows e^q lies in A for every q: generators lie there, e^1=1, and e^(xy)=e^x e^y. MonoidAlgebra.induction_on then puts every algebra element in A, since A is closed under addition and scalar multiplication. Thus A=top, including the empty tuple. The later localization and realization arguments retain their original plans.

source.place: VIII Lemma 3.2.12(ii), proof, printed p.104, affine domain input

proof.text: Put $a=\sum_i p_i$. In $P-\mathbf N a$ the inverse of $p_i$ is $(\sum_{j\ne i}p_j)-a$. Therefore this localization contains all of $P$ and all negatives of its generators, and equals $P^{\rm gp}=L_\eta$. Also $D(a)=\bigcap_iD(p_i)$: the complement of a prime is closed under addition, and is a face by [lem-trf-monoid-prime-minimal-neighborhood]. A prime in this intersection omits every generator, hence is empty. Thus $D(a)=\{\eta\}$ as an open submonoscheme, with its stalk sheaf $L_\eta$. If $n=0$, then $P=\{0\}$, $a=0$, and the same assertions hold with the intersection equal to the whole singleton chart.

Embed $k[P]$ in $k[L_\eta]$ by extending finite coefficient functions by zero; injectivity follows because $P\hookrightarrow L_\eta$ is injective, and the product formula is preserved by addition of exponents. Since $e^a$ is invertible in the group algebra, the formula $f/(e^a)^m\mapsto f e^{-ma}$ defines a ring map from the fraction ring of [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Indeed a fraction equality becomes the same equality after multiplying by the invertible $e^{ka}$, and addition and multiplication obey the displayed fraction rules. This map is injective: $f e^{-ma}=0$ implies $f=0$ by invertibility and the coefficient embedding. It is surjective: every $l\in L_\eta=P-\mathbf N a$ has $l=p-ma$, so $e^l$ has the displayed preimage; a finite sum of such preimages is a preimage of any group-algebra element. It is the claimed $k$-algebra isomorphism. All maps commute with further localization, since on each original monomial and every inverted monomial they have the same values.

source.place: VIII Proposition 3.2.2, localization sentence, and 3.2.4, printed p.103; explicit fraction verification

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b) to the chart $\operatorname{Spec}k[P]$ and $e^a$. Step 6 identifies its open $D(e^a)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}k[L_\eta]$. The realization gluing prescribed in [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] takes $D(b)$ in a monoid chart to the scheme basic open $D(e^b)$, using the monoid localization maps. Step 5 identifies the generic open $\{\eta\}$ in every chart with the same open submonoscheme. It lies in every overlap of charts in $M_\eta$. Restricting the overlap gluing to it gives precisely the identity on its intrinsic stalk $L_\eta$, hence on $k[L_\eta]$. Thus all these open subschemes glue to one open $T_\eta=\operatorname{Spec}k[L_\eta]$, rather than to multiple copies. No chart from a different $M_{\eta'}$ overlaps these charts: otherwise a point in the overlap would have both maximal generalizations. Therefore the quotient-and-sheaf gluing is the disjoint union $X=\coprod_\eta k[M_\eta]$, and each summand is open and closed.

source.place: VIII Proposition 3.2.2 and 3.2.4, printed p.103; basic-open input: Stacks 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine), 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves)

proof.text: In the domain $k[P]$, $(0)$ is a prime belonging to $D(e^a)$, because the monomial $e^a$ is nonzero. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes](1)--(2), its closure is $V(0)=\operatorname{Spec}k[P]$, which is irreducible. Likewise $\operatorname{Spec}k[L_\eta]$ is nonempty and irreducible. Hence $T_\eta$ is dense in every chart of $X_\eta$ and therefore in $X_\eta$: every nonempty open intersects some chart, then its dense torus open. A space with a dense irreducible subspace is irreducible, since any decomposition by two closed subsets restricts to such a decomposition of that subspace, and the closed subset containing it contains its closure. Thus $X_\eta$ is irreducible and nonempty. As in Step 2, irreducibility implies connectedness, and no connected subset can meet two different clopen summands.

source.place: VIII 3.2.4, printed p.103; Stacks 00ES (algebra.tex, lemma-irreducible), parts (1)--(2)

proof.text: A domain is reduced, so each chart scheme is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff]. Every local ring of $X$ is a local ring of one of these open charts, hence is reduced. Therefore $X$ and every $X_\eta$ are reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Combining this with Step 8 and the reduced-and-irreducible characterization in [def-pc-integral-scheme] proves that each $X_\eta$ is integral. Step 8 shows these clopen connected summands are exactly the connected components of $X$. The original finite chart cover realizes to a finite affine cover by finitely generated $k$-algebras, by Step 4; the finite-affine-cover criterion of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] proves that $X$ is finite type over $k$. If $M$ is empty, the realization glues the empty diagram, so it is the empty scheme; reducedness is vacuous, the finite affine cover is empty, and there are no connected components. All other assertions quantify over points or charts and are then vacuous.

Step 1: at most 2^n primes per chart, by the face-generator clause. Step 2: the empty prime lies in every nonempty open of a chart and is chart-independent, because generalizations stay in an open chart; the M_eta form a clopen irreducible partition. Step 3: the stalk at eta is P^gp via the smallest neighbourhood D(sum p_i). Step 4: cancellative and torsion free, so k[P] and k[L] are domains. Step 5: in P[a^-1] the inverse of p_i is (sum of the other p_j) - a, D(a)={eta}, and n=0 is handled. Step 6: explicit isomorphism k[P]_{e^a} to k[L]. Step 7: the gluing on {eta} is the identity on L, so there is one torus, and charts of different M_eta are disjoint. Step 8: (0) lies in D(e^a), so the torus is dense and X_eta is irreducible. Step 9: reduced, integral and finite type. Small cases checked: empty M, P={0}, Z^r, N, the cusp <2,3>, and N glued to itself at the generic point (non-separated). No duplicates: lem-trf-toric-monoid-comparison and the parent lem-trf-toric-realization-finite-type state different things. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem finite_chart_components (M : Fine.{u}) (hM : M.IsTorsionFree) : Finite M.space ∧ Finite (ConnectedComponents M.space) ∧ (∀ x : M.space, ∃! η : M.space, η ⤳ x ∧ ∀ z : M.space, z ⤳ η → z = η) ∧ (∀ C : ToricComponent M, IsClopen {x : M.space | ConnectedComponents.mk x = C.component} ∧ IsGenericPoint C.genericPoint {x : M.space | ConnectedComponents.mk x = C.component} ∧ IsIrreducible {x : M.space | ConnectedComponents.mk x = C.component} ∧ ConnectedSpace {x : M.space // ConnectedComponents.mk x = C.component}) ∧ Set.range (fun C : ToricComponent M ↦ {x : M.space | ConnectedComponents.mk x = C.component}) = irreducibleComponents M.space ∧ (∀ U : AffineOpens M, ∃ C : ToricComponent M, ∀ x : M.space, x ∈ U.1 → ConnectedComponents.mk x = C.component)

reviewed_lean.note: I matched every clause of the node to the four sorried theorems in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.MonoschemeFiniteChartComponents. Covered: finite space; unique maximal generalization (η ⤳ x with maximality); the ConnectedComponents fibres are clopen, irreducible and connected with a generic point, and their range is irreducibleComponents; each chart lies in one component. Generic stalk ≃* lattice equals GrothendieckGroup.of; lattice ≃ ℤ^r; chart completion ≃ lattice through degree; k[P] is a domain and the monomials generate it. faceLocalization(powers a) = ⊤; Localization.Away ≃ₐ k[L] with the e^{q-ma} formula; Spec range = D(e^a); the chart Spec map composed with realizationι equals torusEmbedding; the degree maps are compatible with restriction. Realization: reduced, LocallyOfFiniteType ∧ QuasiCompact (the dependency's record), a coproduct cofan, components in bijection with connected components, IsClosed, IsIntegral, nonempty open irreducible torus whose closure is its component, and the empty case. The M_η fibres agree via uniqueness. No hypothesis is stronger than the node's: the shared universe u for k is forced by the realization definition. Edge cases checked: empty M, n=0, m=0, rank 0, non-separated gluing. Lean statement verbatim and declarations present; the node differs from live only in lean; no definitions, only sorry, docstrings with source and blueprint. Not a duplicate of the parent ToricRealizationFiniteType theorem. Nothing was compiled because no file changed.
